sections.subtopic: Named curricula — the Lower School's strongest detail
sections.preview: Verbatim: > "Trinity Episcopal School develops mathematicians in Kindergarten through Grade 5 using > the Math in Focus 2020 curriculum, which is the U.S. edition of the highly effective > Singapore Math approach." > "…utilizes the Amplify Science units of study as its core curriculum…" Social Studies uses…
sections.text:
Verbatim:
> "Trinity Episcopal School develops mathematicians in Kindergarten through Grade 5 using
> the **Math in Focus 2020 curriculum**, which is the U.S. edition of the highly effective
> **Singapore Math** approach."

> "…utilizes the **Amplify Science** units of study as its core curriculum…"

Social Studies uses **"Storypaths"** units. Literacy covers "phonemic and phonological
awareness" in K–2, with **word study through Grade 5**.

**Naming a specific published curriculum is unusual** on this roster and is the clearest
thing a parent can actually evaluate here.

Students > learn Spanish through the five Cs from the National World…
sections.text:
> ⚠️ **This is on the lower-school-ENRICHMENTS page, not the curriculum page.**

Verbatim:
> "All students are introduced to Spanish as an enrichment class in **grades K-5**, with
> an emphasis on language and culture via the **Descubre el Español** curriculum. Students
> learn Spanish through the **five Cs** from the National World Language Standards:
> Communication, Cultures, Connections, Comparisons, and Communities."

> "They explore not only the language, but also the culture of **20 Spanish-speaking
> countries**."

**For heritage speakers**, the programme "also provides the **Anthologia**", and
"Students in **grades 4-5** access this program at school and at home using student books
and an eLearning center."

**So the language ladder runs K–5 Spanish enrichment → a Level 1 high-school language
(Spanish I or Latin I) completed by the end of 8th grade.**

sections.preview: Verbatim from the 2026-27 School Profile: > "Weekly Enrichments: Lower School- Healthful Living (PE & Wellness), Spanish, > Visual Arts, IDEA (STEM) Lab, Faith Studies, and Music" Six enrichments, published as a fact.
sections.text:
Verbatim from the 2026-27 School Profile:
> "**Weekly Enrichments: Lower School-** Healthful Living (PE & Wellness), Spanish,
> Visual Arts, **IDEA (STEM) Lab**, Faith Studies, and Music"

Six enrichments, published as a fact.

sections.subtopic: ⚠️ Technology — published ONLY in the profile PDF
sections.preview: Verbatim from the 2026-27 School Profile: > "K-8 Technology Program: facilitated by Digital Learning Catalysts" > "1:1 iPads for all students K-1" > "1:1 Chromebooks for all students Gr. 2-8" > ⚠️ Confirmed absent from every curriculum and enrichment web page. iPads, > Chromebooks, the IDEA Lab, Computer Science and…
sections.text:
Verbatim from the 2026-27 School Profile:
> "**K-8 Technology Program:** facilitated by **Digital Learning Catalysts**"
> "**1:1 iPads** for all students **K-1**"
> "**1:1 Chromebooks** for all students **Gr. 2-8**"

> ⚠️ **Confirmed absent from every curriculum and enrichment web page.** iPads,
> Chromebooks, the IDEA Lab, Computer Science and Learning Lab appear on **zero**
> `/academics/` pages. Checked: MS curriculum, LS curriculum, MS enrichments, LS
> enrichments, MS landing, LS landing, student support.
>
> **Cite the profile PDF for every technology claim**, not a curriculum page.

**Digital Learning Catalysts** are named in blog posts — **Mer Leeson** (Lower School) and
**Nikki Dunn** (Middle School).

**The IDEA (STEM) Lab** is the only named academic facility on the entire campus. It
appears in the LS weekly enrichment list and is **not an arts space** (see the Arts file,
where its absence from arts facilities matters).

sections.subtopic: Other whole-school programmes from the profile
sections.preview: Verbatim: > "Workshop Instuctional Model: Collaborative, inquiry- and problem-based learning > experiences, as well as differentiated instruction and lesson design supported by a team > of Learning Catalysts" > ⚠️ "Instuctional" is the school's own typo in the 26-27 PDF (it appears in the > 25-26 edition too).…
sections.text:
Verbatim:
> "**Workshop Instuctional Model:** Collaborative, inquiry- and problem-based learning
> experiences, as well as differentiated instruction and lesson design supported by a team
> of **Learning Catalysts**"

> ⚠️ **"Instuctional" is the school's own typo** in the 26-27 PDF (it appears in the
> 25-26 edition too). Preserve it inside a quotation; do not silently correct it.

> "**K-8 Service Learning:** Curriculum & Community Partnerships, Community Garden and
> **Aquaponics Program**"
> "**K-8 Faith Studies:** Bible lessons, study of world religions, etc."

**Student-to-teacher ratios**, verbatim:
> "**22:2 (K-2), 24:2 (3-5), 20:1 (6-8)**"

> ⚠️ **Note the format.** K–5 is published as a **two-teacher** ratio (22 students to 2
> teachers, 24 to 2), while 6–8 is a conventional 20:1. Copy char-for-char — rewriting
> "22:2" as "11:1" would be a re-typing, and it also loses the real claim, which is that
> every K–5 classroom is **co-taught**.

sections.subtopic: The math track — a real published sequence with five 8th-grade endpoints
sections.preview: Verbatim: > "Students are placed in grade-level and accelerated courses based on specific > performance criteria. Instruction is grounded in a problem-based core curriculum > rooted in content and practice standards to foster learning and achievement for all." > "The following courses are offered: > 6th Grade: Math 6…
sections.text:
Verbatim:
> "Students are placed in grade-level and accelerated courses based on **specific
> performance criteria**. Instruction is grounded in a problem-based core curriculum
> rooted in content and practice standards to foster learning and achievement for all."

> "The following courses are offered:
> **6th Grade:** Math 6
> **7th Grade:** Pre-Algebra and Advanced Pre-Algebra
> **8th Grade:** Foundations in Algebra, Math 1, Algebra 1, Math 2, Geometry"

| Grade | Courses |
|---|---|
| 6 | Math 6 |
| 7 | Pre-Algebra · Advanced Pre-Algebra |
| 8 | Foundations in Algebra · Math 1 · **Algebra 1** · Math 2 · **Geometry** |

**Five distinct 8th-grade math courses** is genuinely differentiated for a middle school,
and it is the clearest "advanced work" signal this school publishes.

> ⚠️ **The placement criteria themselves are NOT published.** The page says placement is
> on "specific performance criteria" and never states what they are. That full sentence is
> the entirety of what exists. **Do not imply the criteria are available.**

sections.subtopic: ⛔ DO NOT SHIP: "Algebra 1 and Geometry for high school credit"
sections.preview: Trinity never says this. The site lists Algebra 1 and Geometry as 8th-grade math courses and says nothing whatsoever about credit. The ONLY explicit high-school-credit claim on the site is the world language.
sections.text:
**Trinity never says this.** The site lists Algebra 1 and Geometry as 8th-grade math
courses and says **nothing whatsoever about credit**.

**The ONLY explicit high-school-credit claim on the site is the world language.**

sections.subtopic: World language — the one genuine high-school-credit claim
sections.preview: Two separate verbatim statements: > "Middle School students choose between Latin and Spanish, completing Level 1, a > high school course, by the end of their 8th Grade year." > "Students will graduate from Trinity having completed Spanish I, a high school level > course, and will be ready for Spanish II should they…
sections.text:
Two separate verbatim statements:

> "Middle School students choose between **Latin and Spanish**, completing **Level 1, a
> high school course**, by the end of their 8th Grade year."

> "Students will graduate from Trinity having completed **Spanish I, a high school level
> course**, and will be ready for **Spanish II** should they choose to continue studying
> the language."

Note the two phrasings differ slightly — the World Language header says "a high school
course", the Spanish paragraph says "a high school **level** course". Quote whichever fits
the context, exactly as published.

**This is the K–8 analogue of "advanced courses"**: a student leaves 8th grade having
completed a high-school Level 1 language.

sections.subtopic: The enumerable MS course list — approximately 26 offerings
sections.preview: Pooled from the MS curriculum page, the MS enrichments page and the profile PDF: Core (9): English/Language Arts · Math 6 · Pre-Algebra · Advanced Pre-Algebra · Foundations in Algebra · Math 1 · Algebra 1 · Math 2 · Geometry Social Studies (3): Geography, Civics & Global Issues (6) · Modern World History (7) · Modern…
sections.text:
Pooled from the MS curriculum page, the MS enrichments page and the profile PDF:

**Core (9):** English/Language Arts · Math 6 · Pre-Algebra · Advanced Pre-Algebra ·
Foundations in Algebra · Math 1 · Algebra 1 · Math 2 · Geometry

**Social Studies (3):** Geography, Civics & Global Issues (6) · Modern World History (7) ·
Modern United States History (8)

**Science (1):** Science, grades 6–8 — integrated, **no per-grade course names published**

**World Language (2):** Spanish I · Latin I

**Enrichments and electives (11):** Art/Visual Arts · PE (Healthful Living, 7) ·
Hebrew Scriptures (6) · Christian Narratives (7) · World Religions (8) · Learning Lab (6) ·
Music Ensembles (6) · Computer Science (7) · Speech & Debate (7) ·
Social Issues Seminar (8) · FOCUS Period (6–8)

**Plus:** Choice Electives (7–8) *(named, contents unpublished)* · a **drama elective** ·
ensembles **choir/band (6)** and **Advanced Band / Advanced Choir (7–8)**

### A forthcoming addition

From the school's AI task force post, verbatim:
> "A **6th Grade technology class will be added to Middle School** as digital learning
> catalysts teach students how to use AI to create code and build, not just how to input
> questions…"

Attribute as **announced**, not current.
